cor.text: Revenues and Cost of Goods Sold . Revenue for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025 was $0 and $0, respectively, and comprised of recognized service revenue. Historically, the Company’s revenue has been generated from sales of the PURE EP™ Platform and related support services; however, commercial activity was not significant during the year ended December 31, 2024 and did not recur in subsequent periods.

rd.text: We anticipate that our results of operations will fluctuate for the foreseeable future due to several factors, such as the progress of our research and development and commercialization efforts, the timing and outcome of future regulatory submissions, and other macroeconomic and operational uncertainties. Due to these uncertainties, accurate predictions of future operations are difficult or impossible to make.

ga.text: General and Administrative Expenses. General and administrative expenses for the three months ended March 31, 2026 were $34,254, an increase of $31,297 or 1059%, from $2,957 incurred in the three months ended March 31, 2025. Stock-based compensation and common stock issued for services totaled $25,370 in the current period, representing approximately 74% of total general and administrative expenses, compared to $2,074 in the prior period, reflecting equity awards issued under consulting, advisory, and service arrangements. Additional increases were driven by higher professional fees, payroll, and compliance-related costs associated with expanded corporate activities during the current period.

nonop.text: Other Income (Expense), net. Other income (expense), net for the three months ended March 31, 2026 totaled $(11,513), compared to other income of $184 for the three months ended March 31, 2025. The change of $(11,697) was driven primarily by the following items, none of which existed in the prior-year period due to the May 2025 acquisition of Streamex Exchange and the November/December 2025 convertible debenture financing:

tax.text: Income taxes (benefit). For the three months ended March 31, 2026, the Company recorded an income tax benefit of $565, compared to $0 in the prior-year period. The benefit resulted from the reversal of a portion of the deferred tax liability associated with the amortization of identifiable intangible assets recognized in the Company’s acquisition of Streamex Exchange Corporation, which is held through the Company’s Canadian subsidiary. Intangible amortization for book purposes creates a temporary difference because such amortization is not deductible for Canadian income tax purposes, resulting in a deferred tax liability that reverses as the book basis of the intangible assets declines. The deferred tax liability was initially recognized as part of the acquisition accounting in May 2025 and is remeasured each period for changes in enacted tax rates and foreign currency translation. No comparable benefit was recorded in the prior-year period as the acquisition had not yet occurred.

net.text: Net Loss Attributable to Streamex Corp. Common Stockholders . As a result of the foregoing, net loss attributable to common shareholders for the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $46,695 compared to a net loss of $2,814 for the three months ended March 31, 2025. The increase in net loss of $43,881 was primarily attributable to the changes in operating expenses, other income (expense), and income tax benefit described above.

da.text: Depreciation and Amortization Expense. Depreciation and amortization expense for the three months ended March 31, 2026 totaled $1,492, an increase of $1,471, or 7005%, over the expense of $21 incurred in the three months ended March 31, 2025, as a direct result of the amortization of the intangible assets recognized from the acquisition of Streamex Exchange. The Company’s intangible assets primarily consist of trade name, developed technology, legal and compliance framework, and patents.

wc.text: As of March 31, 2026, we had working capital of approximately $42,602 and cash of $6,859. For the three months ended March 31, 2026, we used $10,179 in operating activities, used $1,500 in investing activities, and used $1,637 in financing activities, primarily reflecting the repayment of the remaining outstanding balance on the secured convertible debentures of approximately $38.5 million, substantially offset by net proceeds of approximately $37.2 million from an underwritten public offering completed in January 2026.

opex.text: Net loss was $14,551 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, an improvement of $5,817, or 28.6%, from $20,368 for the prior-year period, driven primarily by lower operating expenses and the commencement of gold lease income. After net income attributable to noncontrolling interests of $1 and preferred stock dividends of $2, net loss attributable to common stockholders was $14,554 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $20,372 for the prior year period. Basic and diluted loss per share was $(0.08), compared with $(0.74), based on weighted-average common shares outstanding of 182,015,405 and 27,706,780, respectively. The increase in weighted-average shares reflects the January 2026 underwritten offering, the February 2026 conversion of debenture principal into common stock, and the inclusion of exchangeable shares in basic shares outstanding following our November 2025 stockholder approval.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expense
ga.text: General and administrative expense decreased by $5,975, or 30.2%, to $13,836 for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $19,811 for the prior-year period. The decrease was driven primarily by a $5,003 decrease in stock-based compensation (to $7,117 from $12,120, a 41.3% decrease) and a $3,573 decrease in consulting and platform-development costs, partially offset by increases in marketing and investor relations cost of $1,234, personnel and board-related costs of $704, insurance cost of $498, legal and regulatory cost of $295, and accounting and audit cost of $234, and by decreases in public-company readiness costs of $247 and corporate infrastructure costs of $226. The lower stock-based compensation reflects the timing and vesting of prior-year equity grants, and the higher marketing, personnel, insurance, and professional costs reflect the build-out of our public-company and tokenization functions following the Streamex Exchange acquisition.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense), Net
nonop.text: Total other income, net, was $105 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with total other expense, net, of $3 for the prior-year period. The current-period amount consisted principally of $200 of other income, net (primarily foreign-currency and other individually immaterial items) and a $14 gain from changes in the fair value of marketable securities, partially offset by a $106 realized loss on marketable securities and $3 of net interest expense. Other income, net, is stated after a $172 unrealized loss on our investment in Metalayer, which we measure using the fund’s reported net asset value per share as a practical expedient for fair value.

net.heading: Net Loss and Loss Per Share
net.text: Net loss was $14,551 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, an improvement of $5,817, or 28.6%, from $20,368 for the prior-year period, driven primarily by lower operating expenses and the commencement of gold lease income. After net income attributable to noncontrolling interests of $1 and preferred stock dividends of $2, net loss attributable to common stockholders was $14,554 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $20,372 for the prior year period. Basic and diluted loss per share was $(0.08), compared with $(0.74), based on weighted-average common shares outstanding of 182,015,405 and 27,706,780, respectively. The increase in weighted-average shares reflects the January 2026 underwritten offering, the February 2026 conversion of debenture principal into common stock, and the inclusion of exchangeable shares in basic shares outstanding following our November 2025 stockholder approval.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities was $21,918 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, an increase of $19,525 from $2,393 for the prior-year period, reflecting the expanded scale of operations following the Streamex Exchange acquisition and the launch of the GLDY program. The six-month net loss of $61,245 included significant non-cash items — $32,487 of stock-based compensation, $11,979 of amortization of debt discounts and issuance costs, $3,057 of loss on debenture extinguishment, $2,963 of depreciation and amortization, and a $172 unrealized loss on the Metalayer investment — together with cash outflows for personnel, professional services, platform development, marketing, insurance, and regulatory compliance.

da.heading: Depreciation and Amortization Expense
da.text: Depreciation and amortization expense increased $917, or 165.5%, to $1,471 for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $554 for the prior-year period. The increase resulted primarily from a full quarter of amortization of the trade name, developed technology, legal and compliance framework, and other identifiable intangible assets recognized in the May 2025 Streamex Exchange acquisition. The prior-year period included only approximately one month of amortization following the acquisition date.

sbc.text: Net loss was $61,245 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, an increase of $38,076, or 164.3%, from $23,169 for the prior-year period, driven principally by higher stock-based compensation and the debenture-related interest expense and extinguishment loss recognized in the first quarter of 2026. After preferred stock dividends of $4, net loss attributable to common stockholders was $61,249, compared with $23,185. Basic and diluted loss per share was $(0.34), compared with $(0.95), based on weighted-average common shares outstanding of 177,787,337 and 24,286,234, respectively. Potentially dilutive securities were excluded from diluted loss per share because their effect would have been antidilutive.

wc.text: As of June 30, 2026, we had working capital of approximately $32,841 and cash of $5,605. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, we used $21,918 in operating activities, net cash provided by investing activities was $9,163 and net cash used in financing activities was $1,882.

opex.text: Our material cash requirements over the next 12 months consist principally of operating expenses, including personnel, professional services, marketing, insurance, technology and public-company costs; the settlement of accounts payable and accrued expenses of $3,191 as of September 30, 2026, including $951 of insurance premium financing; the remaining commitment of $217 under the collaboration agreement with the Liquidity Provider, which accrues at $30 per month through May 14, 2027, subject to the agreement’s termination provisions; and operating lease payments of $45 for the remainder of 2026 and $186 in 2027. Beyond the next 12 months, our contractual obligations consist principally of operating lease payments of $680 from 2028 through May 2031. Cumulative dividends of $128 on our Series C Preferred Stock had accrued as of September 30, 2026, and, other than our insurance premium financing obligation, we have no outstanding debt.

costs.text: Our material cash requirements over the next 12 months consist principally of operating expenses, including personnel, professional services, marketing, insurance, technology and public-company costs; the settlement of accounts payable and accrued expenses of $3,191 as of September 30, 2026, including $951 of insurance premium financing; the remaining commitment of $217 under the collaboration agreement with the Liquidity Provider, which accrues at $30 per month through May 14, 2027, subject to the agreement’s termination provisions; and operating lease payments of $45 for the remainder of 2026 and $186 in 2027. Beyond the next 12 months, our contractual obligations consist principally of operating lease payments of $680 from 2028 through May 2031. Cumulative dividends of $128 on our Series C Preferred Stock had accrued as of September 30, 2026, and, other than our insurance premium financing obligation, we have no outstanding debt.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expense
ga.text: General and administrative expense increased by $11,997, or 259.4%, to $16,622 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $4,625 for the prior-year period. Stock-based compensation expense, a noncash expense, increased by $8,460 to $9,302 from $842, reflecting restricted stock unit awards granted to executives, employees and consultants during 2026 and $3,996 of amortization of the fair value of common stock issued in December 2025 under 12-month marketing and capital-markets advisory service agreements, which had no prior-year equivalent. The stock-based compensation amounts discussed in this section are those recorded in our stock-based compensation expense account; the amounts presented in Note 22 — Segment Reporting and in the statements of cash flows also include common stock issued for services and therefore were $872 and $15,560 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively.

da_op.heading: Depreciation and Amortization Expense
da_op.text: Depreciation and amortization expense decreased by $36, or 2.4%, to $1,452 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $1,488 for the prior-year period. The expense in both periods primarily reflects amortization of the trade name, developed technology, legal and compliance framework, and other identifiable intangible assets recognized in connection with the May 2025 acquisition of Streamex Exchange.

prov.heading: Provision for Credit Loss
prov.text: We recognized a $46 provision for credit loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026, with no comparable amount in the prior-year period. The provision represents the allowance for expected credit losses on the unsecured USDC loan receivable from the Liquidity Provider funded in July 2026, measured using a probability-of-default and loss-given-default approach over the loan’s remaining contractual term. See Note 12 — Loan Receivable and Liquidity Support Arrangement.

nonint.text: Our material cash requirements over the next 12 months consist principally of operating expenses, including personnel, professional services, marketing, insurance, technology and public-company costs; the settlement of accounts payable and accrued expenses of $3,191 as of September 30, 2026, including $951 of insurance premium financing; the remaining commitment of $217 under the collaboration agreement with the Liquidity Provider, which accrues at $30 per month through May 14, 2027, subject to the agreement’s termination provisions; and operating lease payments of $45 for the remainder of 2026 and $186 in 2027. Beyond the next 12 months, our contractual obligations consist principally of operating lease payments of $680 from 2028 through May 2031. Cumulative dividends of $128 on our Series C Preferred Stock had accrued as of September 30, 2026, and, other than our insurance premium financing obligation, we have no outstanding debt.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense), Net
nonop.text: Total other expense, net, was $68 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $10,236 for the prior-year period, representing a favorable change of $10,168. The improvement was driven primarily by the non-recurrence of the $10,214 loss from the change in fair value of the derivative liability recognized in the prior-year period. Current-period other income and expense also included $96 of net interest income, including $96 of accretion of the discount on the loan receivable from the Liquidity Provider, partially offset by a $91 realized loss on marketable securities, a $21 loss from changes in the fair value of marketable securities, and $52 of other expense, net.

net.heading: Net Loss and Loss Per Share
net.text: Net loss was $17,460 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $1,876, or 12.0%, from $15,584 for the prior-year period. The increase was driven primarily by higher general and administrative expense, including higher stock-based compensation, partially offset by the favorable change in other income (expense), net. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $17,465 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $15,586 for the prior-year period, after net income attributable to noncontrolling interests of $3 and preferred stock dividends of $2. The $3 attributable to noncontrolling interests represents the noncontrolling interest holders’ time-weighted share, approximately 10.18%, of Streamex Ltd.’s net income of $26 for the three months ended September 30, 2026. Basic and diluted loss per share was $(0.09), compared with $(0.47), based on weighted-average common shares outstanding of 185,350,763 and 33,352,004, respectively. The increase in weighted-average shares reflects, among other factors, the January 2026 underwritten public offering, the February 2026 conversion of debenture principal into common stock, and the inclusion of exchangeable shares in basic shares outstanding following stockholder approval in November 2025.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities was $28,030 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $20,614 from $7,416 for the prior-year period. The increase primarily reflected a $39,953 increase in net loss to $78,704 and a $9,742 unfavorable change in the net effect of operating assets and liabilities, partially offset by a $29,081 increase in noncash reconciling items. Significant noncash adjustments in the current period included $41,789 of stock-based compensation, $11,979 of amortization of debt discounts and issuance costs, $4,415 of depreciation and amortization, and a $3,057 loss on extinguishment of the convertible debentures, partially offset by a $2,938 realized gain on the sale of gold, a $1,653 deferred income tax benefit, and a $497 gain from the change in fair value of the embedded derivative; noncash adjustments also included $45 of liquidity support arrangement expense settled in GLDY tokens. Operating cash flows also included $7,010 of purchases of USDC digital assets, partially offset by a $1,166 increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses and a $514 decrease in prepaid expenses and other assets.

da.heading: Depreciation and Amortization Expense
da.text: Depreciation and amortization expense decreased by $36, or 2.4%, to $1,452 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $1,488 for the prior-year period. The expense in both periods primarily reflects amortization of the trade name, developed technology, legal and compliance framework, and other identifiable intangible assets recognized in connection with the May 2025 acquisition of Streamex Exchange.

sbc.text: Net loss was $78,704 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $39,953, or 103.1%, from $38,751 for the prior-year period, driven principally by higher stock-based compensation and the debenture-related interest expense and extinguishment loss recognized in the first quarter of 2026, partially offset by the non-recurrence of the prior-year derivative charge and the realized gain on the sale of gold. After net income attributable to noncontrolling interests of $3, reflecting the quarterly time-weighted attribution of Streamex Ltd.’s results described in Note 19 — Noncontrolling Interests, and preferred stock dividends of $7, net loss attributable to common stockholders was $78,714, compared with $38,774 for the prior-year period. Basic and diluted loss per share was $(0.44), compared with $(1.42), based on weighted-average common shares outstanding of 180,336,183 and 27,343,190, respectively. Potentially dilutive securities were excluded from diluted loss per share because their effect would have been antidilutive.

wc.text: As of September 30, 2026, we had working capital of approximately $22,036 and cash of $5,476. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net cash used in operating activities was $28,030, net cash provided by investing activities was $14,262 and net cash used in financing activities was $1,012.

capex.text: The Company’s liquidity forecast includes assumptions regarding the timing and availability of its financial resources, the pace of platform-development and commercialization activities, planned operating and capital expenditures, cost-containment measures, and the timing and amount of potential income. Actual results may differ materially from those assumptions.

intro.text: Streamex Corp. (NASDAQ: STEX) is a technology and infrastructure company focused on the tokenization and digitalization of commodity real-world assets. Streamex delivers institutional-grade solutions that bridge traditional finance and blockchain-enabled markets through secure, regulated, and yield-bearing financial instruments.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: We rely on key officers, consultants and scientific and medical advisors, and their knowledge of our business and technical expertise would be difficult to replace.

Our product development program depends upon third-party researchers, including Mayo Clinic, who are outside our control and whose negative performance could materially hinder or delay our pre-clinical testing or clinical trials.

For our first clinical trial for the PURE EP, titled “Novel Cardiac Signal Processing System for Electrophysiology Procedures (PURE EP 2.0 Study)” which commenced in November 2019, we rely on third parties, including TCARF and Mayo Clinic to conduct the patient cases.

In addition, we are party to various license agreements with Mayo, pursuant to which we rely on research and development information, materials, technical data, unpatented inventions, trade secrets, know-how and supportive information of Mayo to develop, make, have made, use, offer for sale, sell, and import licensed products.

The financial impact of U.S. healthcare reform legislation over the next few years will depend on a number of factors, including the policies reflected in implementing regulations and guidance and changes in sales volumes for medical devices affected by the legislation.
The accuracy of the Company ’ s financial reporting depends on the effectiveness of its internal controls over financial reporting.
We intend to rely on a combination of patents, trade secrets, and nondisclosure and non-competition agreements to protect our proprietary intellectual property.
Furthermore, our ability to enforce our patent rights depends on our ability to detect infringement.
Our success also depends upon the skills, knowledge and experience of our scientific and technical personnel, our consultants and advisors as well as our licensors and contractors.
To help protect our proprietary know-how and our inventions for which patents may be unobtainable or difficult to obtain, we rely on trade secret protection and confidentiality agreements.

Our commercial success also depends upon our ability, and the ability of any third party with which we may partner, to develop, manufacture, market and sell our products, if approved, and use our patent-protected technologies without infringing the patents of third parties.
We depend on our collaboration with Mayo Clinic for the research and development of additional advanced features of PURE EP.

Obtaining and maintaining patent protection depends on compliance with various procedures and other requirements, and our patent protection could be reduced or eliminated in case of non-compliance with these requirements.
We rely on a multidisciplinary team (including from management and third-party service providers ) to assess how identified cybersecurity threats could impact our business.

Our future capital requirements will depend on a number of factors, including the progress of our research and development of product candidates, the timing and outcome of regulatory approvals, the costs involved in preparing, filing, prosecuting, maintaining, defending and enforcing patent claims and other intellectual property rights, the status of competitive products, the availability of financing and our success in developing markets for our product candidates.
Our ability to continue operations after our current cash resources are exhausted depends on our ability to obtain additional financing, as to which no assurances can be given.
The Company’s primary source of operating funds since inception has been cash proceeds from sale of common and preferred stock.

We are currently listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market and therefore rely on the definition of independence set forth in the Nasdaq Listing Rules.

s.t: As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s principal sources of liquidity, in addition to cash on hand, include marketable securities of $ 6,779 , digital assets of $ 922 , and its investments in Metalayer, with a carrying amount of $ 2,208 , which is measured using net asset value per share as a practical expedient for fair value.

In January 2026, the Company sold its entire investment in Empress for gross proceeds of approximately $ 10,190 and recognized a realized gain of approximately $ 484 relative to the investment’s December 31, 2025 carrying value.
As of September 30, 2026, our investment in Metalayer had a carrying amount of $2,208, and we held $922 of digital assets, principally USDC.

These items were partially offset by a $2,938 realized gain on the February 2026 sale of previously pledged gold bullion, a $497 gain from the change in fair value of the debentures’ embedded derivative before its derecognition on settlement, a $286 net realized gain on marketable securities (including the gain realized on the sale of our investment in Empress Royalty Corp.), net of a $140 unrealized loss on marketable securities, and $101 of other income, net.

(ii) our investment in Metalayer had a carrying amount of $2,208, consisting of Class A-1 shares of $1,701 and Class D-1 shares of $507; under a side letter executed on October 23, 2026, we may request redemption of all of our investments in Metalayer on any business day, with redemptions of up to $5,000 payable in cash within two business days and amounts above $5,000 paid in additional tranches of up to $5,000 each, timed in coordination with us, subject to applicable law and Metalayer’s anti-money laundering, sanctions and know-your-customer procedures; and (iii) we held a $101 loan receivable, presented as other receivable on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheet, that matur

Other income, net, consisted principally of $394 of dividend income and $156 of foreign-currency gains, partially offset by a $292 decrease in the net asset value of our investment in Metalayer and $152 of realized losses on other investments.
At December 31, 2025, the Company’s marketable securities consisted of its investment in Empress Royalty Corp., which was sold in full during the first quarter of 2026.
Including our Class A-1 and Class D-1 shares at their September 30, 2026 net asset value, our investments in Metalayer totaled approximately $8,208 on a pro forma basis.

We expect to fund these requirements from cash on hand, sales of marketable securities, our USDC holdings, redemptions of our investments in Metalayer under the October 23, 2026 side letter, the return of the loaned assets upon termination or maturity of the loan to the Liquidity Provider and, as market conditions permit, sales of GLDY interests and equity financings, including under the Equity Subscription Agreement, which requires the filing and effectiveness of a registration statement.
The forecast relies on the redemption of our investments in Metalayer and on repayment of the USDC loan to the Liquidity Provider at its July 7, 2027 maturity.
